prompt: A cyclist travels 240 m east in 40 s and then 90 m west in 20 s. Calculate (a) the average speed and (b) the average velocity for the complete journey.

mark_scheme.criterion: Uses total distance 330 m and total time 60 s.

hints: Use total path length for average speed but start-to-finish displacement for average velocity.
The westward part reduces the eastward displacement but still adds to the distance.
solution: Distance = 240 + 90 = 330 m. Displacement = 240 - 90 = 150 m east. Total time = 60 s. Average speed = 330/60 = 5.5 m s^-1. Average velocity = 150/60 = 2.5 m s^-1 east.
teacher_walkthrough: Add both path lengths for distance: 240 m + 90 m = 330 m.
Add both times: 40 s + 20 s = 60 s. Average speed = 330 m / 60 s = 5.5 m s^-1.
Choose east as positive. Displacement = +240 m - 90 m = +150 m, or 150 m east.
Average velocity = 150 m / 60 s = 2.5 m s^-1 east. The smaller magnitude is expected because displacement is shorter than distance.
